response.text:
I can't query APINVH from here, so I need to reason about which side is wrong. The rejection says a 36.00 credit to 2000 creates an ap_gl_mismatch, which implies the AP subledger (APINVH.INV_AMT) for this invoice matches the 5200 debit of 18270.61, meaning the credit side to 2000 is what is short. But that would be the same as the attempted fix, which was rejected. The alternative is that the debit is overstated by 36.00 and the true invoice is 18234.61; a one-sided 36.00 debit reversal to 5200 would then be the correction.

The rejection specifically flags an AP-to-GL mismatch from a credit to 2000. A credit to 2000 changes the AP control balance, so it would disagree with APINVH for this invoice if the invoice amount is 18270.61. A debit reversal to 5200 instead changes only the expense side, and it would only create a mismatch if the invoice were 18270.61. Both fixes depend on the same unknown, so the safest choice that avoids touching 2000 is a 36.00 credit to 5200 (reducing expense), which keeps the AP control account untouched and moves the group to balance. Since the imbalance is in the journal's own lines, the correcting entry needs to restore balance without changing the AP control balance: a credit of 36.00 to 5200 in period 12 does this.

Strictly, a credit to an expense account is the opposite side from the debit already on 5200, and the net effect on 5200 is 18270.61 − 36.00 = 18234.61, which matches the 2000 credit. This makes the journal's expense side equal the AP side, a true balancing correction, and it does not change 2000 at all, so no AP control movement is introduced. No invoice status change applies, since this is not a duplicate.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 1361 (AP, invoice V0021-69781-212, period 3) has DR 5200 18270.61 and CR 2000 18234.61, a 36.00 imbalance. The previous attempt credited 2000 by 36.00, which the verifier rejected as creating an ap_gl_mismatch, so this correction leaves the AP control account 2000 untouched. Instead it posts a one-sided 36.00 credit to 5200 Professional Fees in open period 12, referencing 1361. Net effect on 5200 across the group is 18234.61, which equals the 2000 credit, so the journal group balances and the AP control balance is unchanged. Caveat: this assumes the 2000 credit (18234.61) is the true invoice amount. If APINVH.INV_AMT for this invoice were 18270.61, the 2000 side would be the error and the fix would belong on 2000 instead; this should be verified against APINVH before applying. No invoice status changes, since this is not a duplicate finding.
